definition.precision/recall/f1: token-level micro-averaged P/R/F1 over the corpus (0-1)
definition.attack_embedding_convention: vec2text attack-convention embeddings E = T5 encoder last_hidden_state mean-pool (corrector.inversion_trainer.call_embedding_model), NO sentence-transformers Dense projection and NO L2 normalisation -- finding F14. data/passage_emb.npy (ST GTR embeddings, Dense+normalised) is NOT used as the attack input because vec2text reconstructs garbage from it even without encryption.

attack_modes.plaintext: invert the plaintext attack-convention embedding E_i (paper 'w/o Enc')
attack_modes.caprise_raw: invert the CAPRISE ciphertext e'_i directly (norm ~ s*||E_i|| ~ 1.5-3, out of the inversion model's input distribution; naive attacker)
attack_modes.caprise_rescaled: invert e'_i * (||E_i||/||e'_i||): attacker restores the original per-vector norm; strongest attack, used for the main Table II row

w/o Enc.note: paper 'w/o Enc' row: plaintext attack-convention embeddings

CAPRISE.note: paper-closest CAPRISE row: raw ciphertext e' fed to vec2text (no rescaling)

CAPRISE_rescaled_attack.note: strongest-attacker row (not in the paper): e' * ||E||/||e'|| restores the original norm; upper bound on reconstruction

findings.row: CAPRISE raw ciphertext (paper Table II analogue)
findings.conclusion: Vec2Text reconstruction collapses when the raw CAPRISE ciphertext is fed to the inversion model (paper-closest attack setting): BLEU drops by more than half

a scale-normalising adversary (e'*||E||/||e'||) recovers much of the reconstruction ability -- the strongest attacker, reported as the privacy upper bound (F3/A11); CAPRISE still degrades it relative to plaintext

findings.note: paper does not state num_steps/beam/N/passage length (A11); our CPU/MPS budget and N=20 may explain the delta

findings.row: CAPRISE raw ciphertext (paper Table II analogue)

findings.conclusion: raw ciphertext (norm ~ s*||E||) is out of the inversion model's input distribution and is much weaker than restoring the original norm; the rescaled attack is the conservative (attacker-favourable) main setting

Vec2Text gtr-base operates on T5 mean-pooled (un-Densed, un-normalised) embeddings; using sentence-transformers GTR embeddings as attack input produces garbage even without encryption (F14), so the attack baseline here is the correct vec2text convention.
